title: U.S. House · Tennessee's 1st District
area: Northeast Tennessee, including Kingsport, Bristol, and Johnson City

context.text: Incumbent Diana Harshbarger (R) advanced unopposed from the August 6, 2026 Republican primary. Kristi Burke won the Democratic primary. The district's 2026 Cook Partisan Voter Index is R+29, and forecasters rate the general election Safe/Solid Republican.

candidates.name: Diana Harshbarger
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced unopposed from the August 6, 2026 Republican primary

summary.text: Diana Harshbarger is the Republican incumbent U.S. Representative for Tennessee's 1st District, a licensed pharmacist and business owner from Kingsport who first took office in January 2021 after winning the open seat. She serves on the House Energy and Commerce Committee, where she is vice chair of the Health Subcommittee, and is seeking re-election in November 2026.

background.text: Born in Bloomingdale, Tennessee, a community outside Kingsport; according to her official biography, she was the first in her immediate family to graduate from high school and college.
Attended East Tennessee State University and earned a Doctor of Pharmacy degree from Mercer University College of Pharmacy.
Returned to the Kingsport area after graduation to start a business, and has been a licensed pharmacist and business owner for over three decades, according to her official biography.
Served as a board member of the International Academy of Compounding Pharmacists.
Won the August 6, 2020 Republican primary and the November 2020 general election for the open 1st District seat, succeeding Rep. Phil Roe, and took office January 3, 2021.
In the 117th Congress (2021-2022) she was assigned to the Homeland Security and Education and the Workforce committees; since 2023 she has served on Energy and Commerce.

In the 119th Congress she serves on Energy and Commerce as vice chair of the Subcommittee on Health and as a member of the Subcommittees on Oversight and Investigations and on Energy, and co-chairs the Congressional Bipartisan Rural Health Caucus and several other caucuses.

Her official biography says she teaches Sunday school, helps with her church's mission work, belongs to the local Chamber of Commerce, and lives in Kingsport and on a farm in Unicoi with her husband, Robert; she has one son and two grandsons.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Energy and Commerce (2025-2026), including its Subcommittees on Commerce, Manufacturing, and Trade; Health; and Energy.

summary.text: Kristi Burke is the Democratic nominee for Tennessee's 1st District, an independent muralist, digital content creator, and local organizer. She won the August 6, 2026 Democratic primary, and describes her campaign as a challenge to policies that she says put corporate profits ahead of residents' needs such as healthcare and housing.

background.text: Says she was raised with a foundation in the church and taught to care for the vulnerable.

Her career experience includes working as an independent muralist, digital content creator, and local organizer, according to Ballotpedia; in her Candidate Connection survey she says she has worked in the beauty industry, painted large-scale murals, and built a YouTube platform focused on critical thinking.
Describes herself as a renter without health insurance who has spent years working to climb out of debt.
Won the August 6, 2026 Democratic primary with 76.6% of the vote, ahead of David Kerr Jr. and Herman Garcia.

priorities.text: Says essential needs like healthcare, housing, and a clean environment should not be gatekept by wealth, and frames her campaign as a challenge to policies that prioritize corporate interests over working residents.

positions.summary: Campaign message emphasizes that healthcare should not depend on wealth and says no one in the district should be 'one medical emergency away from ruin.'
positions.quote: I believe that essential needs like healthcare, housing, and a clean environment, should never be gatekept by wealth.

summary.text: Joshua Ray Ashburn is an independent candidate who says he is not a career politician and is running because he is tired of career politicians being re-elected. He says he supports term limits, stronger border security, small businesses and farmers, and less U.S. involvement in foreign conflicts.

background.text: Says he is 36 years old and a father of two, and has been with his spouse for almost six years.
Describes himself as not a career politician; his Ballotpedia profile lists no prior elected office or career details, and he reports no endorsements.

priorities.text: Says he strongly supports term limits and putting 'the people first instead of politics.'

summary.text: Chris Campbell is an independent candidate who says he has spent his career supporting manufacturers. He is running on restoring domestic manufacturing, patient-directed healthcare, opposition to tariffs, and term and age limits for federal officeholders.

background.text: According to his Candidate Connection survey, he grew up in southwestern Virginia, where he watched furniture and textile factory closures affect his community, and moved to Tennessee in 1991.
Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Tennessee, Knoxville.

Says he has spent his professional career supporting manufacturers in their efforts to remain competitive in a global economy, and that his father worked a bread route while his mother worked in textiles and automotive manufacturing.

priorities.text: Wants to restore domestic manufacturing and 'reshoring' of industries, and supports patients' rights to pursue treatments their providers recommend without insurer denial.

positions.summary: Says tariffs have made housing, energy, groceries, and transportation more expensive and supports abolishing them.
positions.quote: These are fueled by tariffs (taxes) that were unconstitutionally imposed on Americans and a war that we should have never taken part.

summary.text: Richard Baker is a perennial independent candidate who has run for this seat in multiple previous elections (2020, 2022, and 2024). No campaign platform statements were found for the 2026 race.
Billy Cody is an independent candidate on the November 3, 2026 general-election ballot for Tennessee's 1st District. No campaign website or public policy statements were found.
Tyler McClain is an independent candidate on the November 3, 2026 general-election ballot for Tennessee's 1st District. No campaign website or public policy statements were found.
